items.title: Bill Crow interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: You know, Stephen Foster songs, World War I songs, stuff like that.

ctx.x: Well you know in the 20s and 30s, everybody at least sang. I remember singing almost everywhere I went. If we went to church we sang. If we went to an American Legion meeting we sang. If we went to somebody’s house within a half hour after dinner we would be around the piano singing the songs everybody knew. You know, Stephen Foster songs, World War I songs, stuff like that. And everybody sang. There was no such thing as somebody without a voice. There were people that it was understood they didn’t have strong…

together like that. Everybody appreciated barber shop harmony and that sort of thing, and when you got into a big band and could play riffs together or could read dumb stock together and really make it into some music, that was a thrilling achievement.
